title: Private Pilot Syllabus

gradingScale.label: Introduced
gradingScale.meaning: CFI demonstrated it, or the student flew it with a lot of help.

gradingScale.label: Practiced
gradingScale.meaning: The student flies it with some coaching. Safe, but not yet consistent.

gradingScale.label: Proficient
gradingScale.meaning: The student flies it alone and consistently meets the Done when standard. For checkride tasks, that means ACS tolerances.

principles: Lessons have names, not lesson numbers. The order shown is the recommended order.
A lesson is finished when its Done when line is met. If it isn't met, the lesson repeats. If it is, the student moves on, even on the first try.
Each skill is taught once. After that it rides along in later flights.
The CFI can carry 1 or 2 weak items into the next flight as a warm-up instead of repeating a whole lesson.
Items marked Practiced get finished during later lessons. Before solo, every emergency item and stall recovery must be Proficient.

runningThrough.name: Hood time
runningThrough.detail: A few minutes on most flights, starting in Slow Flight & Power-Off Stalls, until 3 hours are logged.

runningThrough.name: Knowledge test
runningThrough.detail: Taken any time before the mock oral.

runningThrough.name: Night block
runningThrough.detail: Flown whenever the season makes it practical.

stages.name: Pre-Solo
stages.summary: Control of the airplane, emergencies, the pattern, and first solo at KBMC. Ends with a stage check flown by another CFI.

flightLessons.name: Intro & Four Fundamentals
flightLessons.objective: Preflight, start, taxi, run-up, and the four fundamentals: straight and level, climbs, descents, and turns, all in one lesson.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student preflights with the checklist and little help, taxis with good directional control, and holds altitude ±200 ft and heading ±20° in straight and level flight and in 30° bank turns.
homework: Read the POH normal procedures for the airplane

flightLessons.name: Slow Flight & Power-Off Stalls
flightLessons.objective: Fly slow flight and recover from power-off stalls, using CRAAC before each maneuver.
flightLessons.doneWhen: Slow flight held at ±100 ft, ±10° heading, +10/−0 kt. Power-off stalls recognized and recovered promptly with minimum altitude loss, with positive rate verified before retracting the last two flap settings.
briefing: Recovery: reduce AOA, level the wings, add power
Just enough aerodynamics to fly safely (G8 comes later)
flightLessons.hood: Introduce straight and level under the hood

flightLessons.name: Power-On Stalls & Steep Turns
flightLessons.objective: Recover from power-on (departure) stalls and fly 45° steep turns.
flightLessons.doneWhen: Power-on stalls recovered without a secondary stall. Steep turns hold ±100 ft, ±10 kt, ±5° bank, and roll out ±10° of entry heading.
briefing: Load factor and why stall speed rises in a turn

flightLessons.name: Emergencies
flightLessons.objective: Handle engine failures, forced landings, and other in-flight emergencies.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student runs ABCD from memory, sets up a simulated forced landing to a reachable field, flies an emergency descent, and works through the POH checklists for at least two system failures.
briefing: ABCD: Airspeed, Best place to land, Checklist, Declare

flightLessons.name: Pattern & Normal Landings
flightLessons.objective: Fly the traffic pattern at KBMC and make normal takeoffs and landings.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student flies the pattern within ±100 ft of pattern altitude, makes correct CTAF calls, runs GUMPS, and lands safely with only occasional verbal help.
briefing: Pattern entry on the 45 to downwind
Power and configuration by leg (1,700 RPM abeam the numbers in the 100i)

flightLessons.name: Go-Arounds, Slips & Crosswind
flightLessons.objective: Go around from a bad approach, slip to a landing, and handle crosswinds.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student lands consistently without CFI input, goes around on their own when an approach isn't stabilized, and uses a forward slip to lose altitude on final.
briefing: Wind correction on takeoff and landing

flightLessons.name: Pattern Emergencies
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student makes the runway from a simulated engine failure abeam the numbers (power-off 180) on most attempts, and states the engine-failure-after-takeoff plan before every departure.
briefing: Engine failure after takeoff and why not to turn back at low altitude
Runway incursion or traffic on the runway

flightLessons.name: Pre-Solo Written & Stage Check
flightLessons.objective: Pass the pre-solo written and a stage check with another CFI.
flightLessons.presoloWritten: Written by the CFI to cover 61.87(b): the Part 61 and 91 rules that apply, the airspace and procedures at KOGD and KBMC, and the airplane's flight characteristics and limitations. Missed answers reviewed and corrected to 100%.
steps: The student departs KOGD alone on the radios, with proper communication.
On the way to KBMC: slow flight, stalls, and an emergency.
At KBMC: a few touch-and-gos, including one simulated engine-out 180.
Back to KOGD for the landing.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The stage check CFI signs off that the student is safe to solo.

flightLessons.name: First Solo
flightLessons.objective: The student's first solo at KBMC.
steps: Fly dual to KBMC for 2 or 3 laps.
The student flies 3 takeoffs and landings to a full stop.
flightLessons.cfiNote: Solo flights from KOGD to KBMC later also need the 61.93(b)(1) endorsement (another airport within 25 nm).

groundModules.name: Airports & Radio
covers: CTAF vs. tower and ground calls
oralCheck: What does a hold short line look like, and from which side can you cross it?
What's the difference between a mandatory sign and a location sign?
Make the initial call to Ogden Ground for a VFR departure to the north.
What does a steady red light mean on the ground? In the air?
When and where do you make CTAF calls at KBMC?

groundModules.name: ForeFlight Setup & Use
covers: Airport pages and the Chart Supplement
oralCheck: Find KOGD's tower frequency and runway lengths.
Turn on the TFR layer. Is anything active near us today?
Pull up the METAR and TAF for KBMC.
Open the checklist for today's airplane.
Connect to the airplane's ADS-B and show me traffic.

groundModules.name: Local Airspace & KOGD Ops
groundModules.due: Before Emergencies (start after Slow Flight & Power-Off Stalls)
covers: Hill AFB (KHIF) Class D and its traffic
Standard departures and arrivals between KOGD and KBMC
Which airspace a student solo can and can't enter
sources: Salt Lake City sectional and SLC Terminal Area Chart
oralCheck: Show me on the chart where the SLC Bravo floor is over Ogden and what altitudes keep you out of it.
What do you need to enter Hill's Class D, and who do you talk to?
Brief your departure from KOGD to KBMC, including which airspace you pass through.
What's required to enter Class B? Can you do it as a solo student?
Which MOAs or restricted areas are nearby, and how do you check whether they're active?

groundModules.name: Checking Weather
oralCheck: Decode this morning's KOGD METAR.
What does an FM group in a TAF mean?
What's the crosswind component for today's runway at KBMC?
What are the weather and wind limits on your solo endorsement?
Go or no-go for a pattern flight right now? Why?

groundModules.name: Traffic Patterns & Landings
covers: KBMC pattern and typical runway use
Stabilized approach criteria and when to go around
sources: Airplane Flying Handbook: traffic patterns; approaches and landings
oralCheck: Describe the recommended way to enter the KBMC pattern.
What are your stabilized approach criteria?
Name three reasons you'd go around.
How do you correct for a left crosswind on final and in the flare?
A larger airplane just landed ahead of you. Where is its wake, and how do you avoid it?

groundModules.name: Emergencies & ADM
oralCheck: Your engine quits at 3,000 ft AGL. Walk me through ABCD.
What's best glide speed in this airplane?
What are your first actions for an electrical fire?
Run IMSAFE and PAVE for today's flight.
Name the five hazardous attitudes and their antidotes.

groundModules.name: Airplane & Systems
covers: Engine, fuel, electrical, and vacuum/pitot-static systems
100i vs. 172 differences (e.g., no carb heat in the 100i)
sources: PHAK: Aircraft Systems; Flight Instruments; Flight Manuals
oralCheck: What documents need to be on board? (SPARROW)
What inspections make this airplane airworthy? (AAV1ATE)
Trace the fuel from the tank to the engine.
The alternator fails. What do you see, and what do you do?
The pitot tube gets blocked. Which instruments are affected, and how?

groundModules.name: Aerodynamics
sources: PHAK: Principles of Flight; Aerodynamics of Flight
Airplane Flying Handbook: slow flight, stalls, and spins
oralCheck: Can you stall at any airspeed? Explain.
Why does stall speed go up in a steep turn?
Name the four left-turning tendencies.
What causes a spin, and how do you recover?
What is ground effect, and where do you feel it?

groundModules.name: Solo Regs prep
oralCheck: Name three things a student pilot can't do under 61.89.
What's the day VFR fuel reserve requirement?
Two airplanes are converging at the same altitude. Who has the right-of-way?
What are the VFR weather minimums in Class D?
What's the minimum altitude over a congested area?

gates.name: Pre-Solo Written
gates.detail: Taken after G1–G8 and the Solo Regs prep. Missed answers reviewed and corrected to 100%.

stages.name: Cross-Country
stages.summary: Ground reference, short and soft field, airspace, navigation, solo cross-countries, and the night block.

flightLessons.name: Ground Reference Maneuvers
flightLessons.objective: Fly the rectangular course, S-turns, and turns around a point with correct wind correction.
flightLessons.doneWhen: Altitude ±100 ft, airspeed ±10 kt, a steady ground track, and correct entry and exit headings.
briefing: Picking a safe reference with forced landing options

flightLessons.name: Short & Soft Field Takeoffs and Landings
flightLessons.objective: Fly short field and soft field takeoffs and landings to ACS standards.
flightLessons.doneWhen: Short field landings touch down on or within 200 ft past the chosen point at POH approach speed. Soft field takeoffs and landings keep weight off the nosewheel with no unwanted touchdowns or settling.

flightLessons.name: Local Solo Practice
flightLessons.objective: Build solo time and finish Practiced items.
flightLessons.eachFlight: The CFI assigns 1 or 2 specific items and checks them on the next dual flight.
flightLessons.doneWhen: No fixed end. Fly as needed toward 10 hours of solo.

flightLessons.name: Towered Ops & Local Airspace
flightLessons.objective: Operate confidently at KOGD and around Hill AFB and the SLC Bravo.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student handles all KOGD tower and ground communications alone, gets and uses flight following, and plans a route around or under the Bravo without CFI input.
briefing: "Cleared into the Class Bravo" and when you need it

flightLessons.name: Dual Cross-Country (Wendover)
flightLessons.objective: Fly a full cross-country from KOGD to Wendover and back, planned by the student.
flightLessons.doneWhen: The student flies the nav log within ±3 min of ETAs, opens and closes a flight plan, completes a diversion to an alternate, and runs lost procedures.
inFlight: Pilotage and dead reckoning, cross-checked with VOR and GPS
A simulated diversion partway through the route
Lost procedures (Climb, Communicate, Confess, Comply, Conserve)
Hood: unusual attitude recoveries and a 180° turn out of simulated IMC
Mountain flying and density altitude considerations on the route
briefing: UTTR and Dugway restricted areas along the route (check status before every flight)

flightLessons.name: Solo Cross-Countries
flightLessons.objective: Fly solo cross-countries that the student plans alone.
flightLessons.beforeFirst: Ground gate met, plus the 61.93(c)(1) endorsement.
flightLessons.eachFlight: The CFI reviews the plan and gives the 61.93(c)(2) endorsement for that flight.
flightLessons.doneWhen: 5 hours of solo cross-country logged, counting the long solo cross-country.
flightLessons.note: Finish at least 3 solo full-stop takeoffs and landings at KOGD (towered) on any of these flights.

flightLessons.name: Long Solo Cross-Country
flightLessons.meets: 61.109(a)(5)(ii): at least 150 nm total, full-stop landings at 3 points, one leg over 50 nm straight-line (KOGD–KENV about 96 nm).
briefing: UTTR and Dugway restricted areas west of KTVY
SLC Bravo on the KTVY–KOGD leg
flightLessons.doneWhen: Flight complete and logged with the endorsement.

nightBlock.note: Fly whenever the season makes it practical. In winter, as early as the end of Stage 1 once the student is ready for the pattern.

lessons.name: Night Local
lessons.objective: Night pattern work, night emergencies, and night vision and lighting.
lessons.doneWhen: The student lands safely at night without CFI input and handles a simulated electrical failure.

lessons.name: Night Cross-Country
lessons.objective: A night cross-country over 100 nm total distance.
lessons.doneWhen: Over 100 nm total. Across the night block: 3 hours of night and 10 full-stop takeoffs and landings.
briefing: SLC Bravo transition, or the route around it

groundModules.name: Student Pilot Regs
groundModules.due: Before Local Solo Practice to KBMC (first module of the stage)
oralCheck: What has to happen before you can fly solo to an airport more than 25 nm away?
What does your solo cross-country endorsement have to say?
You're flying a magnetic course of 260°, more than 3,000 ft AGL. Which cruising altitudes can you use?
When are you required to use oxygen?
Where do you need ADS-B Out?

groundModules.name: Airspace & Charts
oralCheck: What are the VFR weather minimums in Class E above and below 10,000 ft MSL?
What's the difference between a restricted area and a MOA?
What does a magenta vignette mean on the sectional?
Find KENV in the Chart Supplement. What's the CTAF and fuel availability?
How do you check for TFRs along your route?

groundModules.name: Weather Theory & Services
sources: PHAK: Weather Theory; Aviation Weather Services
oralCheck: What makes air stable or unstable, and what clouds go with each?
What weather comes with a cold front passing through?
What's the difference between AIRMET Sierra, Tango, and Zulu?
Read me the winds aloft at 9,000 ft for SLC.
What signs of mountain wave would you look for?

groundModules.name: Performance & W&B
sources: PHAK: Weight and Balance; Aircraft Performance
oralCheck: Figure today's density altitude at KOGD.
What's the takeoff distance over a 50 ft obstacle today?
Run a weight and balance with you, me, and full fuel.
Does the CG move forward or aft as fuel burns in this airplane?
How does high density altitude change your takeoff and climb?

groundModules.name: Navigation & Planning
covers: ForeFlight planning: filing, nav logs, performance, W&B
oralCheck: Figure true heading and groundspeed for a leg using the E6B.
How do you open and close a VFR flight plan?
You need to divert right now. Walk me through it.
You're lost. What are the 5 Cs?
How do you tell which way to turn to intercept a VOR radial?

groundModules.name: Mountain Flying
sources: FAA Tips on Mountain Flying pamphlet
PHAK: density altitude and mountain weather
oralCheck: Why do you cross a ridge at an angle?
Where would you expect downdrafts with a west wind over the Wasatch?
When would you cancel a mountain flight because of wind?
What's your escape plan if you're in a canyon and the terrain rises faster than you can climb?
How does density altitude change your plan for a hot afternoon departure from KENV?

groundModules.name: Night & Aeromedical
oralCheck: Why do you look slightly off-center at night?
What's the black hole illusion, and how do you counter it?
What extra equipment is required for night VFR?
How do you turn on pilot-controlled lighting at KBMC?
What do you need to carry passengers at night?

gates.name: Solo Cross-Country Planning
gates.detail: The student plans the whole flight alone (nav log, weather briefing, W&B, performance, go/no-go) and briefs it to the CFI. CFI then gives the 61.93(c)(1) endorsement.

stages.name: Checkride Prep
stages.summary: Bring every ACS task to Proficient. Ends with a mock oral and a mock checkride flown by another CFI.

flightLessons.name: ACS Review & Checkride Prep
flightLessons.objective: Bring every ACS task to Proficient.
flightLessons.eachFlight: The CFI picks only tasks still at Introduced or Practiced. Proficient tasks are not re-flown unless they slip.
flightLessons.requirement: At least 3 hours within the 2 calendar months before the checkride (61.109(a)(4)).

flightLessons.name: Mock Checkride
flightLessons.objective: A full checkride profile flown by another CFI, run like the real one.
profile: Plan and start a cross-country (e.g., to KENV)
flightLessons.doneWhen: Every task rated at ACS standards. Tasks that don't meet ACS go back to ACS Review for just that task.

groundModules.name: Private Pilot Regs & Maintenance
sources: PHAK: Flight Manuals and Other Documents
oralCheck: A friend offers to pay for the whole flight. Can you accept? Why or why not?
What do you need to carry passengers?
The landing light is inoperative. Can you go? Walk me through 91.213.
Show me the last annual and 100-hour in the logbooks.
When do you have to notify the NTSB?

groundModules.name: ACS Walk-Through
covers: Every knowledge and risk management element in the Private Pilot Airplane ACS, tied back to G1–G16
oralCheck: The Mock Oral is the oral check for this module.

knowledgeTest.timing: Any time before the Mock Oral.
knowledgeTest.before: Sporty's course plus the CFI's knowledge test endorsement (61.35(a)(1), 61.103(d)).
knowledgeTest.after: CFI reviews every missed ACS code with the student.

gates.name: Mock Oral
gates.detail: Full mock oral covering the ACS. Pass when the student can answer, or find the answer for, every element without coaching. Weak areas go back to the matching G module before the Mock Checkride.

requirements.name: Long solo cross-country (150 nm, 3 points, one leg over 50 nm)
Solo full-stop takeoffs and landings at a towered airport

endorsements.name: Student pilot certificate issued (IACRA) and medical in hand
Solo flight, first 90 days (limits written in)
Solo flight renewal every 90 days, as needed
Solo takeoffs and landings at another airport within 25 nm (e.g., KBMC)
Pre-solo night flight training (only if soloing at night)
Repeated solo cross-country within 50 nm (if used)
Solo in Class B (only if used)
Review of missed knowledge test areas
Prep within the preceding 2 calendar months
Practical test: flight proficiency and aeronautical experience
8710 application completed in IACRA and logbook reviewed
